examiner_answers.question: Q3. There is no meter-to-transformer map. How do you know which homes share a transformer?
examiner_answers.note: build_transformers permutes homes, cuts groups of k and draws count groups without replacement; load_map refuses a meter under two transformers. Claims hold.

examiner_answers.question: Q4. How big is each transformer, and what counts as overloaded?
examiner_answers.note: rate() is today's group peak times margin, overload_metrics flags any hour above limit x rating; margins and limit read from config; unity power factor is stated in rate's docstring. Config line refs had moved and were updated.

examiner_answers.question: Q5. Where does the 2030 load come from?
examiner_answers.note: Draw rules and session sampling match the code, but the answer left out that both devices come off one random order, so 97.91% of new heat pump homes also get a new EV. Added, with the drawn-apart result.

examiner_answers.question: Q6. Your teammate says most overloads are heat pump nights, yet EV staggering fixes most of them. Which is it?
examiner_answers.note: fair_shares is a correct two-load Shapley split, but the answer read hours_lead_ev (argmax, ties to EV) as 'EV larger'. Reworded with the strict share 19.42%, the both-needed share 76.0% and the 95.38% that clear with no new EV.

examiner_answers.question: Q7. What does staggered charging do, and does it lose any energy?
examiner_answers.note: stagger_slots ranks EVs per transformer modulo the window hours, so a transformer with more EVs than window hours reuses slots; the answer said each gets its own slot. Wording now says round robin. Energy is computed before the move (delivered_hours x charger kW) and the test checks it.

examiner_answers.question: Q8. Is the battery model physical, or does it just subtract kW?
examiner_answers.note: dispatch.py discharges min(load above ceiling, power, charge above floor, host draw when no export), charges only into room under the ceiling, capped by power and free capacity, and stores inn x efficiency. Claims hold.

examiner_answers.question: Q11. A battery lasts 15 years and a transformer 30. How do you compare their cost?
examiner_answers.note: capital_recovery_factor and deferral_value match the stated formulas; every price is read from config; the review script rebuilt 51.92% and the $7,730 tie on its own annuity math.

examiner_answers.question: Q12. How do I know a number on the page or in a doc was not typed by hand?
examiner_answers.note: record() is the one writer; trace_numbers fails a number that matches no fact or config input. Caveat: it matches any of about 1,800 keys at the shown precision, so a typed number can pass by coincidence (in this review a typed 1.5 traced to a sizing margin). The claim as written holds.

examiner_answers.question: Q13. Where does customer data go?
examiner_answers.note: record(private=True) writes outputs/private/facts_private.json, .gitignore line 21 ignores outputs/private/, and the review script prints aggregates only. Claims hold.

examiner_answers.question: Q15. Random groups change with the seed. How stable are the results?
examiner_answers.note: build_transformers seeds its generator; the widest seed gap in facts is 1.37 points against the 1.5 tolerance in config; the review's own seeds 101 to 105 land within tolerance of every simulated fact.
